entities.name: Abgar V
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abgar V, called Ukkāmā, was an Arab King of Osroene with his capital at Edessa and described as 'king of the Arabs'.

Born in unknown circumstances, Abgar V ascended to the throne around 42 CE after the death of his father, Abgar IV. His reign marked a significant period in the history of Osroene, a kingdom that played a crucial role in the ancient Near East.

Abgar V's significance lies in his efforts to promote Christianity among the Arab population, which led to the conversion of many Jews and Gentiles to Christianity.

He also expanded the borders of Osroene through military campaigns, establishing trade relations with neighboring kingdoms. However, his reign was cut short when he died in 50 CE.

Abgar V's legacy can be seen in the continued presence of Christianity in the region and the impact of his policies on the surrounding kingdoms.

The Edict of Milan, issued by Emperor Constantine in 313 CE, recognized Christianity as a legitimate faith, paving the way for its spread throughout the Roman Empire. This, in turn, was influenced by Abgar V's efforts to promote Christianity in Osroene.
